We need to produce a test class for NumericIndicator.min(Number) method. The method signature: public NumericIndicator min(Number n) { return min(createConstant(n)); } So it returns a NumericIndicator that is the min of delegate and constant indicator of n. The class also has min(Indicator<Num> other). So we need to test both static (Number) and dynamic (Indicator) maybe. But the focal method is min(Number). So test that min with a constant works correctly.

We need to follow template using JUnit5 and Mockito.

We need to set up dependencies: NumericIndicator requires a delegate Indicator<Num>. In tests we can use a mock Indicator or use actual ClosePriceIndicator with a MockBarSeries as in existing tests.

We need to import necessary classes: org.ta4j.core.indicators.numeric.NumericIndicator, org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.ClosePriceIndicator, org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.VolumeIndicator maybe not needed, org.ta4j.core.BarSeries, org.ta4j.core.num.Num, org.ta4j.core.mocks.MockBarSeries, java.util.function.Function, etc.

We need to use numFunction for converting numbers to Num. In existing test class they use AbstractIndicatorTest which provides numFunction. But here we have a simpler test class; we can just use a simple Num implementation. In ta4j, there is a default implementation of Num maybe DecimalNum. We can import org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum; but not sure. The library includes interface Num and implementations. Could use DecimalNum.valueOf(double). Usually use DecimalNum.valueOf(1). So we can use DecimalNum.

But we need to create a BarSeries with MockBarSeries. The MockBarSeries constructor takes Function<Number, Num> numFunction and varargs double values. In the existing test they have a field numFunction from AbstractIndicatorTest. In our test we can create a lambda: n -> DecimalNum.valueOf(n.doubleValue()).

So in setupBeforeEach we create series, closePriceIndicator, numericIndicator.

We need to test min with static number: numericIndicator.min(5) returns a NumericIndicator. Then we verify that its getValue at index i equals min(cp1.getValue(i), constant 5). The constant is Number n, but constant indicator returns same constant for any index.

Implementation: NumericIndicator.min(Number n) calls createConstant(n) which likely returns ConstantIndicator of Num. So min returns NumericIndicator that returns min between delegate and constant.

So test: for some indices, compute expected = cp1.getValue(i).isLessThanOrEqual? Actually min should return the smaller of the two numbers. So we can compute expected = cp1.getValue(i).min(constantNum). But Num interface has min method? Actually Num may have min(Num other). Let's assume there is a method min(Num). But not sure. Could use cp1.getValue(i).isLessThan(other) ? then cp1.getValue(i) else other. Simpler: we can compare double values.

We can convert to double via cp1.getValue(i).doubleValue() and compare with 5. Then expected = Math.min(value,5). Then use assertEquals with DecimalNum.valueOf(expected). Use assertEquals? Use assertEquals from JUnit with expected Num compare using equals.

Better to use assertEquals(expectedNum, result.getValue(i)). Since DecimalNum implements equals based on value.

Thus test.

Also test dynamic: numericIndicator.min(Indicator) maybe not needed but we can include.

But requirement: "Make sure not to invoke any private methods or fields of the target class and dependent class." That's fine.

Now implement test class.

Now implement:

@BeforeAll static void setupBeforeAll() {} maybe nothing.

@BeforeEach void setupBeforeEach() { create series, cp1, numericIndicator = NumericIndicator.of(cp1); }

Need fields: BarSeries series; ClosePriceIndicator cp; NumericIndicator numericIndicator; Function<Number, Num> numFunction;

Initialize numFunction = n -> DecimalNum.valueOf(n.doubleValue());

Series: new MockBarSeries(numFunction, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6); maybe more values.

Now test method:

@Test void min_withNumber_returnsSmallerValue() { NumericIndicator minIndicator = numericIndicator.min(4); // constant 4

for i 0.. series.getBarCount()-1 compute expected = Math.min(cp.getValue(i).doubleValue(), 4.0); assertEquals(DecimalNum.valueOf(expected), minIndicator.getValue(i)); }

Also test that min with constant lower than all values returns constant across all indices. Eg constant -10.

Also test that min with constant higher than all values returns delegate values.

Potentially also test that min returns NumericIndicator with delegate being MinValueIndicator? Not needed.

Add assertions: assertNotSame(numericIndicator, minIndicator);
